nodes.label: A 49-year-old woman has facial ulcers, including healed lower lip and nasal dorsum ulcers and a nonhealing left infraorbital ulcer

Patient reported several years of facial ulcers described as 'scratches' developing over weeks to months into red, indurated, tender ulcers that finally crusted and healed; healed ulcers were present on the lower lip and nasal dorsum, with a nonhealing ulcer in the left lateral infraorbital area
Review of systems was positive for dry mouth, Raynaud phenomenon, morning joint pain, mild hand and ankle swelling, and dysphagia

Later examination revealed diplopia, a sense of fullness below the left eye, restriction of the left eye into hypotropic and exotropic positions, full-thickness defect through the lateral lower eyelid, and exposed conjunctiva and bony orbital rim
Positive ANA, low C4, and elevated ACE
Orbital biopsy shows granulomatous inflammation with polarizable foreign-body material and negative cultures
Nasal septal perforation and saddle nose are present
No trauma or injection history identified to explain exogenous foreign material
No trauma, injection, or other exposure source identified despite exhaustive history retrieval
Expert analyses note that autoimmune serologic findings and saddle nose are nonspecific and may be secondary to the foreign-body granulomatous reaction
Autoimmune serologic abnormalities and saddle nose are secondary phenomena of the foreign-body granulomatous reaction
